run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T23:07:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a chain that bottoms out at the cart service's Redis dependency. frontend-proxy returned HTTP 504 on span_name "ingress" after its 15 s upstream timeout; the error rate was ~0 before the rate window ending 23:07:49 and then 0.533/s, rising to 0.99-1.29/s. The cause one hop down is frontend's calls to oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and /AddItem hanging, which in turn is cart failing to reach Redis: cart's own spans and logs report "Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis" from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() line 97. Affected, each with its own evidence: frontend-proxy (504 ingress spans), frontend (500 on /api/cart), cart (FailedPrecondition error spans and error logs), checkout (own error-rate series and 15 s p95 from 23:13:49) and load-generator (504 client spans). The deepest supported cause is pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr, the endpoint cart cannot use; that attribution stays a hypothesis because the valkey-cart container produced no readable logs, defines no probe, and Cilium policy objects for the cart-to-valkey path could not be read. Checked and healthy: all five nodes, cilium-agent agents and coredns pods, product-catalog (p95 ~1.9 ms), and ad/recommendation/accounting/payment/fraud-detection, whose error series showed only sparse blips also seen before 23:05 or stayed at zero.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span error rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, grouped by span_name and status_code) was 0 for span_name="ingress", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" through the rate window ending 23:06:49 apart from sporadic 0.011-0.022 blips, then 0.533/s at 23:07:49 and 0.992-1.285/s from 23:11:49 to 23:16:49, while ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET fell from 7.855/s at 23:06:49 to 2.466-2.822/s afterwards.

The frontend-proxy error spans are operation "ingress" with status tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR" and durations 15,000,011-15,000,896 us; their child spans "router frontend egress" last the same ~15 s with http.status_code="0", which the metric records as STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so the 504 is a proxy timeout rather than an HTTP error returned by frontend.

The latency sits on the frontend-to-cart hop: frontend p95 reached 15000 ms for span_name "grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart" and "grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem" from 23:09:49, for "GET /api/cart", "POST /api/cart" and "executing api route (pages) /api/cart", and for the "POST"/"GET" server spans at 23:07:49, while frontend's "grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct" (30-80 ms), "grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations" (3.9-155 ms) and "grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" (3.9-145 ms) stayed fast.

Cart's own server spans are the failing hop and name Redis: operation "POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart" and "POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem" carry error=true, otel.status_code="ERROR" and the description Status(StatusCode="FailedPrecondition", Detail="Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() in /usr/src/app/src/cartstore/ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 97"), with durations 476,482,345-479,682,021 us.

Cart's Redis client spans stop at the onset: p95 for cart span_name "HGET", "HMSET", "EXPIRE", "POST" and "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean" is present through the rate window ending 23:07:49 (HGET 1.94 ms) and absent from 23:09:49 onward, while cart's "POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart" and "POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem" p95 becomes 15000 ms at 23:09:49.

Cart pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logged "Connection failed. Disposing the object" at 2026-11-16T23:05:51.9403003Z, then repeated "Wasn't able to connect to redis" (first in the 22:40:00-23:09:00 window at 2026-11-16T23:08:08.139444Z), each followed by "Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised." and still occurring at 23:14:25.

The client-visible failures are generated above cart: frontend spans "GET /api/cart", "POST /api/cart" and "executing api route (pages) /api/cart" have error=true, http.status_code="500", otel.status_code="ERROR" with grpc.error_message "9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: Can't access cart storage ... Wasn't able to connect to redis" and durations about 499-501 s, while the load-generator's paired client spans carry http.status_code="504" after 15 s.

Per-service error-span rates rose for frontend-proxy (0.533 at 23:07:49, then 0.99-1.29/s), frontend (0.111 at 23:09:49, then 0.265, 0.400, 0.333), cart (0.088-0.133/s from 23:09:49) and checkout (0.0667/s at 23:13:49 and 23:15:49), while ad and recommendation showed only sparse 0.011-0.014 blips also present before 23:05 and accounting, payment and fraud-detection stayed at 0.

The Redis dependency object: pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is Running with container valkey-cart ready, restartCount 0, lastState empty, running since 2026-11-16T22:34:46Z at pod IP 100.96.2.228 on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae; Deployment valkey-cart is generation 1 with 1/1 ready and available replicas, image docker.io/valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine, limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi, and it defines no livenessProbe, readinessProbe or startupProbe. Cart's env is VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, Service valkey-cart (port 6379, targetPort 6379) has endpoint address 100.96.2.228 for that pod, and cart's pod IP 100.96.2.233 is on the same node.

valkey-cart's container is not resource-starved: working set 3.48-4.42 MB against the 10Mi limit, container_memory_failcnt 0, CFS throttled-period ratio about 1-6% before and 5-7% after 23:07, and CPU about 0.0017-0.0024 cores until 23:07:30 rising to 0.0030-0.0040 cores afterwards.

Cart container cart-755465879b-t9mf7 grew from 59.9 MB working set at 23:03:49 to 81.7 MB at 23:07:49 and 97.4 MB at 23:13:49 (limit 165Mi, container_memory_failcnt 0), its CFS throttled-period ratio rose from 0.12-0.27 before to 0.853-0.935 at 23:09:49-23:15:49, and its CPU rate fell to 0.0023-0.0040 cores at 23:07:30-23:08:00 before rising to 0.017-0.032 cores from 23:08:30.

Cluster infrastructure shows no fault: all 5 nodes (including i-0146cb0d0caf26bae) are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False, and kube-system pods including cilium-agent cilium-kvgq8 on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae and both coredns-b5494cbf4 pods are Running with restartCount 0 since 2026-11-12.

The only otel-demo events in the window belong to the old pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s: Pod Killing (count 75, first 2026-11-15T10:07:13Z, last 2026-11-16T23:10:39Z, "Stopping container cart") and Warning FailedKillPod (count 30, last 2026-11-16T23:10:38Z, "error killing pod: failed to KillContainer for cart ... DeadlineExceeded").

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and start times 2026-11-16T22:34:37Z-22:34:39Z (cart-755465879b-t9mf7 22:34:37Z, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-6rwg6 22:34:37Z, frontend-675fd7b5c5-hbqcn 22:34:38Z, checkout-5dccddf8bb-pkwzl 22:34:37Z), and cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s is no longer present.

ConfigMap flagd-config key demo.flagd.json has every fault-injection flag at defaultVariant "off": adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure.

The fault originates in the valkey-cart Redis instance, pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr behind Service valkey-cart:6379: cart's established connection to it was lost at 23:05:51 and reconnection never succeeded for the rest of the observed window, so every cart GetCart/AddItem blocks and then fails with FailedPrecondition. Supporting evidence: cart's own error text names EnsureRedisConnected(), cart's Redis client spans disappear after 23:07:49, and the valkey container never restarted and roughly doubled its CPU after 23:07:30 while staying far below its memory and CPU limits. Not confirmed: the container emitted no readable log lines and has no probe, so whether Redis was blocked, loading or rejecting connections could not be observed.

Alternative candidate that cannot be excluded: connectivity between the cart pod (100.96.2.233) and valkey-cart (100.96.2.228:6379) was blocked or dropped at the network layer at 23:05:51. The cluster runs Cilium and defines the CRDs ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io and ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io, but their objects could not be read with the available resource kinds, so policy state for these two pods during the window was not observed.

valkey-cart did not crash and the cluster was not under pressure: its pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, its working set (3.48-4.42 MB) and CFS throttling (5-7%) are far from its 10Mi/10m limits, container_memory_failcnt is 0, and all nodes plus cilium agents and coredns are healthy, so a valkey crash, OOM or node-level outage is not what the evidence shows.

Only the cart path failed while other dependencies of the same requests were healthy: in the same traces the frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" span to frontend and frontend's "grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct" calls returned http.status_code="200" / rpc.grpc.status_code="0" with 119-1,649 us durations, and product-catalog p95 stayed near 1.9 ms across the window.

frontend-proxy as the origin is rejected: its ingress spans are 15 s 504 timeouts whose paired egress span to frontend runs the same 15 s, and the FAILED_PRECONDITION "Wasn't able to connect to redis" detail is carried by cart's own spans and passed up through frontend, so frontend-proxy exposes a downstream failure rather than producing one.

Cart CPU throttling or memory growth as the trigger is rejected: cart's CPU rate fell to 0.0023-0.0040 cores at 23:07:30-23:08:00 while calls were already hanging on Redis, its throttle ratio only climbed to 0.853-0.935 from 23:09:49, and the first explicit Redis failure ("Connection failed. Disposing the object") was logged at 23:05:51, before both.

A flagd fault-injection flag is rejected as the cause: every variant in ConfigMap flagd-config key demo.flagd.json is defaultVariant "off" (including cartFailure, paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable), and the observed failure is a Redis connectivity error thrown from ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected(), not an injected application error response.

The terminating old cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s is rejected as this cause: its Killing/FailedKillPod history started 2026-11-15T10:07:13Z (counts 75 and 30) long before the window, its cart container held a flat 29,138,944 byte working set with zero CFS throttling throughout the window, and its final kill at 23:10:38-23:10:39 followed the Redis failure that began at 23:05:51 without changing the failure pattern.

Inspect the valkey-cart container directly (redis-cli -h valkey-cart PING, INFO clients/commandstats/persistence, SLOWLOG GET, blocked_clients, LATENCY) and retrieve its stdout from node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, then add a readiness/liveness probe such as redis-cli ping to Deployment valkey-cart, because Ready currently only means the container process exists and said nothing about serving Redis.

Inspect the in-cluster Cilium state for the cart and valkey-cart endpoints around 23:05:51 (cilium-dbg endpoint list, cilium-dbg monitor or hubble flows for 100.96.2.233 to 100.96.2.228:6379) to confirm or rule out an egress/ingress drop, since Cilium policy CRDs exist but were not readable in this Run.

Reduce the amplification risk in the cart service: its 45m CPU limit and the synchronous EnsureRedisConnected() reconnect path turned a Redis connection loss into ~480 s hangs and thread-pool starvation; make reconnection asynchronous with circuit breaking, set short RPC deadlines, and re-evaluate the cart CPU limit.

gaps: valkey-cart container logs returned no lines for 22:30:00-22:40:00 and for 22:55:00-23:23:52 (views 501f5e6a-feb8-4ea9-ae3d-75cc3b30a021, 86c1ae72-a687-460e-9674-b2a5277d68c1, 5cb1e6e4-0b05-4891-b5ff-592c56533ab1 all no_data), so whether Redis was loading, blocked on a command, out of clients or erroring internally is unknown.

Cilium policy objects (CRDs ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io, ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io) exist but cannot be read with the available resource kinds, so any policy applied to cart or valkey-cart around 23:05:51 is unverified.
The core NetworkPolicy query for namespace otel-demo returned no objects in a no_data view (a6032073-f253-4601-861c-c5e51107687c), which cannot prove that no policy existed at 23:05:51.

The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not loaded in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with {severity="warning"} both returned no_data (8a84086c-0df2-4e9d-b815-45f447dce1e0, 4446841f-4ebb-4b1b-984d-8799f5936009), so the rule expression, threshold and current firing state could not be verified.

kube-state-metrics series returned no_data (get_metric_names {__name__=~"kube_.*"} view 5a79d819-2136-429f-b4e3-b65cfde7451d and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment=~"cart|valkey-cart"} view 55d814cb-4186-4923-a2a4-28ffbb79a91c), so pod ready/restart history from kube-state-metrics is unknown.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines in 23:05:00-23:16:00 (views 3ab325ac-bce3-4ad4-b0c4-d6ac84e41444, a392d7fd-23fe-47a2-a89f-2058abf939b9 no_data) and checkout's 381 log lines matched none of the error/cart/timeout keywords (view 535c0c0a-659b-49ac-9c81-2802e96b31d1), so their application-level error text is unknown beyond the spans.

Telemetry for all otel-demo services stops between 23:15:49 and 23:17:49 (all rate series go to 0 or NaN and cart logs read through only to 23:14:25), so whether the cart-to-valkey connection recovered and the state after that is unknown.

Traces searches for error=true on service frontend and service cart in 23:07:49-23:23:52 returned no_data (views cede3c00-bd61-4253-af6f-99c99f99577b, 20a66e63-0111-4f41-838b-4c635739ba63), and a mean-duration query over cart span_name using _sum/_count returned no_data (0b817466-4226-4cff-8fab-6b945acf2f24); those views neither add nor subtract from the findings.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no record of configuration, deployment or network-policy changes at 23:05:51 could be checked.
Secrets cannot be read, so any credentials involved in the cart-to-valkey connection (for example Redis AUTH) could not be verified.
next_steps: Run redis-cli against valkey-cart from the cart pod and from another pod to separate 'Redis not serving' from 'cart-to-valkey path blocked', and read the valkey container stdout from node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae.
Check Cilium endpoint and policy state (cilium-dbg endpoint list, cilium-dbg monitor or hubble) for cart 100.96.2.233 and valkey-cart 100.96.2.228:6379 around 23:05:51.
Add readiness/liveness probes to Deployment valkey-cart and export Redis metrics so that Ready reflects command serving rather than container existence.
Re-check with fresh telemetry after 23:17:49 to confirm whether frontend-proxy ingress 504s and cart Redis errors cleared and whether the root cause was a transient Redis stall.
Review the RequestErrorRate rule definition in the source that produced the alert, since it is not present in this Prometheus's loaded rule groups.

Alternative candidate that cannot be excluded: connectivity between the cart pod (100.96.2.233) and valkey-cart (100.96.2.228:6379) was blocked or dropped at the network layer at 23:05:51. The cluster runs Cilium and defines the CRDs ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io and ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io, but their objects could not be read with the available resource kinds, so policy state for these two pods during the window was not observed.

recommendation.text: Inspect the valkey-cart container directly (redis-cli -h valkey-cart PING, INFO clients/commandstats/persistence, SLOWLOG GET, blocked_clients, LATENCY) and retrieve its stdout from node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, then add a readiness/liveness probe such as redis-cli ping to Deployment valkey-cart, because Ready currently only means the container process exists and said nothing about serving Redis.

Inspect the in-cluster Cilium state for the cart and valkey-cart endpoints around 23:05:51 (cilium-dbg endpoint list, cilium-dbg monitor or hubble flows for 100.96.2.233 to 100.96.2.228:6379) to confirm or rule out an egress/ingress drop, since Cilium policy CRDs exist but were not readable in this Run.

Reduce the amplification risk in the cart service: its 45m CPU limit and the synchronous EnsureRedisConnected() reconnect path turned a Redis connection loss into ~480 s hangs and thread-pool starvation; make reconnection asynchronous with circuit breaking, set short RPC deadlines, and re-evaluate the cart CPU limit.

counter_evidence.text: valkey-cart did not crash and the cluster was not under pressure: its pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, its working set (3.48-4.42 MB) and CFS throttling (5-7%) are far from its 10Mi/10m limits, container_memory_failcnt is 0, and all nodes plus cilium agents and coredns are healthy, so a valkey crash, OOM or node-level outage is not what the evidence shows.

Only the cart path failed while other dependencies of the same requests were healthy: in the same traces the frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" span to frontend and frontend's "grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct" calls returned http.status_code="200" / rpc.grpc.status_code="0" with 119-1,649 us durations, and product-catalog p95 stayed near 1.9 ms across the window.

rejected_hypothesis.text: frontend-proxy as the origin is rejected: its ingress spans are 15 s 504 timeouts whose paired egress span to frontend runs the same 15 s, and the FAILED_PRECONDITION "Wasn't able to connect to redis" detail is carried by cart's own spans and passed up through frontend, so frontend-proxy exposes a downstream failure rather than producing one.

Cart CPU throttling or memory growth as the trigger is rejected: cart's CPU rate fell to 0.0023-0.0040 cores at 23:07:30-23:08:00 while calls were already hanging on Redis, its throttle ratio only climbed to 0.853-0.935 from 23:09:49, and the first explicit Redis failure ("Connection failed. Disposing the object") was logged at 23:05:51, before both.

A flagd fault-injection flag is rejected as the cause: every variant in ConfigMap flagd-config key demo.flagd.json is defaultVariant "off" (including cartFailure, paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable), and the observed failure is a Redis connectivity error thrown from ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected(), not an injected application error response.

The terminating old cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s is rejected as this cause: its Killing/FailedKillPod history started 2026-11-15T10:07:13Z (counts 75 and 30) long before the window, its cart container held a flat 29,138,944 byte working set with zero CFS throttling throughout the window, and its final kill at 23:10:38-23:10:39 followed the Redis failure that began at 23:05:51 without changing the failure pattern.
